summary: The diff narrows tight_task_validation.py's contradiction detector from whole-document bag-of-words overlap to a local, windowed cluster-overlap check that excludes tokens near negation/qualifier phrases, which can only shrink the set of matches (fewer false positives) while a dedicated true-positive test confirms real unconditional conflicts are still caught; I traced the four false-positive patterns and the true-positive case by hand against the algorithm and they behave as claimed, and all 6 new pytest cases pass. The auto_phase_continuation.py surfacing change was verified end-to-end against task-gateway.py's actual fail() JSON shape (error/reason/guidance keys) and wires correctly, only adding an informational note on an already-failing path with no change to control flow or dispatch behavior. No files under .github/workflows/**, migrations/, schema.*, auth/, .env, or security/permission/payment/billing/rls paths are touched, consistent with the pre-assigned tier1 classification. One non-blocking architecture note: the module's own docstring says it must stay a faithful line-for-line port of src/lib/task-tightening.ts so the TS (app/HTTP) and Python (shell-fleet) enforcement points apply identical rules, but that TS file is not present in this repo and was not updated alongside this fix -- if it exists in a sibling repo, the two validators have now diverged and a human should port the same fix there.
issues: Docstring's stated invariant (this Python module must mirror src/lib/task-tightening.ts line-for-line) is not upheld by this diff since the TS file isn't in this repo/wasn't updated -- flag for a human to port the same fix to the TS original if it still exists, to avoid the two enforcement points silently drifting.
